sentences.text: Coram:

HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE SWARANA KANTA SHARMA  ORDER % 18.04.2023 CRL.M.A. 10049/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 0611/2020 registered at Police Station Palam Village, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/354/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Notice.
Mr. Anand V. Khatri, learned ASC accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.
M.P.S. Kasana and Investigating Officer (IO), SI Naveen Saini Police Station, Police Station Palam Village, Delhi.
6.

entities.text: Naveen Saini Police Station, Police Station Palam Village
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that on 24.04.2012, the marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
Two children were born out of the said wedlock.

Due to some matrimonial disputes, respondent no. 2 had lodged a complaint against the petitioners and on the basis of the said complaint, an FIR bearing No.
Sanjeev Kumar & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166370048/
1 0611/2020 was registered at Police Station Palam Vilalge, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/354/406/34 of IPC.

entities.text: Sanjeev Kumar & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is stated that during the pendency of the case, both the parties have amicably settled all their disputes vide Compromise Deed dated 06.08.2022.
7.

On the query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled/compromised between them and they have been living together since 06.08.2022.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that she has no objection if FIR may be quashed.
8. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

9. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 0611/2020 registered at Police Station Palam Village, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/354/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
10. The present petition stands disposed of.
11. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J APRIL 18, 2023/
